preconditions: Select base checkup, doctor, fresh machine audit, save or PR-comment formatting; these paths differ.
Resolve the project, host metadata scope, discovery permissions and report audience for the current task.
Read the infra_advisor and llm_backends declarations when an audit can refresh the shared registry. Parent-local hashes do not bind those modules.

expected_effects.effect: run assembles project directives, metrics, static scans, runtime prefix facts and drift findings.
expected_effects.scope: Selected project source/configuration, local catalogs and host/runtime metadata; caller memory/stdout.
expected_effects.basis: run calls auto_audit, metrics.collect and bounded summary helpers. policy_committed tests file existence rather than Git tracking.
expected_effects.impact: Uses CPU/I/O and can reveal paths, snippets and setup details. Unavailable analyses and CI wiring exemptions limit what an empty findings list establishes.
expected_effects.verification: Run against a fixture project with a policy file that is not Git-tracked; check existence reporting, unavailable sections and selected evidence scope.

expected_effects.effect: Base checkup may refresh discovery through infra_advisor; doctor may also refresh via its machine audit.
expected_effects.scope: llm_backends discovery targets and its toolkit-local registry, plus host hardware profiling.
expected_effects.basis: run calls auto_audit; gather refreshes on empty registry. doctor calls audit(fresh=machine_fresh), which also refreshes an empty registry.
expected_effects.impact: An audit can probe endpoints and overwrite shared registry entries. With no discovered backends, multiple parents can independently repeat discovery.
expected_effects.verification: Run fixture checkup with mocked discovery and a temporary empty registry; inspect saved entries and verify later cached reads avoid discovery.

expected_effects.effect: --save persists the report; --pr-comment formats Markdown for stdout and returns before the save path.
expected_effects.scope: The selected project .botte/reports or the stdout recipient, including configured CI consumers.
expected_effects.basis: main calls report.save only after the early pr_comment return. format_pr_comment is a formatter; posting belongs to the GitHub workflow.
expected_effects.impact: Retains analysis details and consumes storage. A zero CLI exit or a formatted no-drift headline alone does not certify all checks or installation health.
expected_effects.verification: Mock a report with drift, request PR-comment plus save and assert no report write; inspect output and exit status independently.

downstream_effects.effect: Inherited discovery writes can affect later routing or another audit.
downstream_effects.scope: Other callers using the shared llm_backends registry.
downstream_effects.basis: checkup depends on infra_advisor and optional machine audit; those may replace registry contents.
downstream_effects.impact: A parent audit can change later backend choices, even though it never fixes project code itself.
downstream_effects.verification: Compare the registry before and after an isolated parent audit and identify the dependency that performed the write.

downstream_effects.effect: CI or another caller may publish the report or use drift/recommendations to decide follow-up actions.
downstream_effects.scope: PR readers, saved report recipients and any subsequent task resources.
downstream_effects.basis: The workflow posts formatted output; main returns reports and recommended commands without executing repairs.
downstream_effects.impact: Incomplete findings can be overinterpreted and metadata disclosed. CI-specific wiring exemptions do not transfer to a local installation.
downstream_effects.verification: Review actual analyzer availability, checkout identity, runtime context and output audience before publication or a downstream decision.

reversibility.strategy: Reconcile inherited registry writes and saved reports separately. The checkup supplies findings, not an automatic code repair or rollback; published copies follow the publishing system.
residual_effects: Probe traffic and report disclosures can persist after local report removal.
Changes made by a consumer of the findings need their own recovery evidence.

retry.check_before_retry: Check partial analyzer results, registry state and saved outputs. Cached and fresh reruns can observe different environments and repeat discovery or report writes.
retry.stop_condition: Stop repeated probing or persistence on an unresolved failure. Resolve unavailable evidence proportionally rather than executing suggested fixes to make a headline green.

required_scope: Existing task authorization for the project and host metadata, inherited discovery range and report persistence. Publishing a PR comment is a separate caller action using its existing authorization.

analysis.summary: The checkup composes useful local diagnostics but also inherits discovery and optional persistence effects. Its availability flags, context exemptions and output mode matter when interpreting the verdict.
uncertainties: infra_advisor, llm_backends, metrics, context_profiler, scanners, fix and report are not covered by this skill-local hash set.
Some optional analyses can be unavailable; a successful process exit does not authenticate findings or prove task completion.
policy_committed indicates file presence only, and BOTTE_CHECKUP_CONTEXT=github-pr changes wiring applicability.

reuse.target: Use a scoped checkup snapshot as one input to integration review.
reuse.rationale: Common diagnostics and explicit availability/context fields help compare changes while keeping operational conclusions separate.
adaptations: Keep the exact checkout and runtime context with the report.
Preserve unavailable checks and compare inherited state writes as well as findings.
Require task-specific evidence for completion and review the publication audience.
reuse.validation: Replay cache-hit/cache-miss and unavailable-analysis fixtures, then compare actual target evidence before using the report in a merge or deployment decision.
